question_text: What is the redox concept? Give an example.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: A redox reaction is a chemical reaction in
which oxidation and reduction take place
steps.why: Electrons lost by one species must be gained by another, so oxidation can never happen without reduction. That pairing is the redox concept.
common_mistakes: Defining only oxidation or only reduction. The concept is the two happening together.
steps.memory_tip: Red-ox: REDuction and OXidation in one word because they happen in one reaction.
steps.margin_note: Both half-processes and the word simultaneously must appear.

steps.label: The example
steps.why: The zinc-copper reaction shows both halves in one line: the two electrons zinc loses are exactly the two copper gains.
common_mistakes: Writing the equation without labelling which species is oxidised and which is reduced.
Reversing the labels: the electron LOSER is oxidised.
steps.memory_tip: OIL RIG — Oxidation Is Loss of electrons, Reduction Is Gain.
steps.margin_note: Label oxidation and reduction on the equation; the labels carry the mark.

insider_note: The example earns its mark only when the two oxidation-number changes are labelled on the equation — the bare equation is treated as half an answer.
